findings.title: A due box that a reviewed or sending chain has reserved, withdrawn by the due run: no test fails without it
findings.scenario: I dropped withdrawDueNow's reserved filter and every test still passed. No test lets a box come due while a chain reserves it: neither a chain kept for Send (a public Mix my boxes again review, held up to BUILT_TTL_MS = 10 min) nor one being sent. A regression that withdraws such a box would ship green. The review's Send would then be refused for a spent input, or a withdraw would race the chain for one box.
findings.evidence: Change in the copy: lovejoin.ts:6876 `const candidates = free(inPool(back, pool), reserved);` became `const candidates = inPool(back, pool);`. The lane's guess (b18), tests/lovejoin-bring-review-fixes.test.ts: 21 passed. Then I ran the 41 tests in 8 files that execute this line (lovejoin.test.ts, lovejoin-pools, lovejoin-restore, lovejoin-reward-balance, lovejoin-flows, lovejoin-merged-review, lovejoin-retire-review-fixes, lovejoin-crediting-review-fixes), filtered with -t: all passed. I also placed a marker that logs whenever `free(...)` drops a candidate and has no other effect. It never fired across the full fire-marker run, so no test ever has a reserved box among the due ones. The sibling checks are pinned: Bring one back's (7034) by lovejoin-bring-review-fixes.test.ts:524, and Bring every box back's (7277) by lovejoin-bring-all-back.test.ts:371.
findings.fix: Add a test in lovejoin.test.ts 'the boxes' withdraws'. Give the wallet one box that is due, and let publicAgainBuild keep a Mix again for Send that spends it. withdrawDue('preprod', false, now) should return [], with t.koios.submitted unchanged and the box's due time kept. publicSubmit should then succeed.
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/ for reservedBoxes, boxReserved, 'reserved' near withdrawDue, and 'mutant'. Nothing records this. Backlog's 'Untested in 1.8.0' line is about withdrawDueNow's re-arm, which is a different line.

findings.title: A withdraw whose signed hash differs from the reviewed build, sent anyway: no test fails without the hash check
findings.scenario: I deleted the check and every test still passed. Every test's finishLovejoinWithdraw or signScriptSpend fake returns the transaction's own hash, so the check never fires. A regression that drops it would ship green, and so would a later finishing step that alters the body. Today finish_withdraw only adds giveme.my's witness over the unchanged body, so nothing makes the two hashes differ.

findings.fix: In lovejoin-withdraw-submit.test.ts's due(), add a variant whose finishLovejoinWithdraw returns txHash '00'.repeat(32). withdrawDue should return [] with nothing submitted, kept(t).withdrawing undefined and the due time kept. The same class exists, not mutated here: sessions.ts:4477 and script-spend.ts:429 throw worker.spend.signingChanged, and no test names that key either.

findings.title: A copy of the 5 ₳ pool taken as a return's ADA and collateral pool: no test fails without adaPoolOf's copy check
findings.scenario: I dropped `!p.copy` from adaPoolOf and every test still passed. In no call anywhere in the suite does the copy check change the pick. No test gives discovery a copy of the 5 ₳ values that would be found before the shown pool, or in its place. A regression would therefore ship green and send a return's spare ADA and its session's collateral into a copy that no wallet shows.
findings.evidence: Change in the copy: lovejoin.ts:701-702 `pools.find((p) => !p.token && p.ref && !p.copy && !isRetired(p) && p.lovelace === COLLATERAL_LOVELACE)` with `!p.copy` removed. The lane named no test. I ran the 73 tests in 6 files that call adaPoolOf and deal with copies or the 5 ₳ pool (lovejoin-merged-review, lovejoin-share-review-fixes, lovejoin-round2-retire, lovejoin-found-later, lovejoin-retired, lovejoin-round2-sessions): all passed. A marker comparing the original pick with the mutant's never saw them differ, across the 342 tests in 41 files that call adaPoolOf. The other three conjuncts are pinned (see checked_ok).
findings.fix: In lovejoin-share-review-fixes.test.ts's 'the 5 ₳ pool a return and its collateral go into' block, add two cases. If discovery hands over only a copy of the 5 ₳ values ({ copy: ref }), adaPool() is undefined and the return's collateral comes back directly. If the copy is listed before the shown pool, the shown pool is the one picked.

findings.title: A session chain keeps its reservation after the network's check refused it: no test fails without the unreserve (both copies)

A refused review then keeps its pool boxes reserved for BUILT_TTL_MS (10 minutes). The next review, or another chain, finds them taken and builds fewer boxes or leaves Lovejoin out.

notes: Method. 71 mutants over the 37 merged guards: one per check, the smallest change that removes it, each made in a copy and put back after its run. Step 1 ran each mutant against the files the lane named, whole, with --bail=1. Step 2 used a second copy with markers that change no behaviour. Each marker logged when its mutant would change what the code does: the guard's condition true, or the mutated predicate picking differently. I ran that copy over the 192 test files that import the four modules directly or through src/, minus 43 files that never call a Lovejoin flow. Each survivor was then run against exactly the tests in which its marker fired. A guard whose marker never fired cannot fail any test. M01, M02, M03, M09, M14, M62 and M68 were also run against every test that merely reaches the line, and all passed.

Load. The machine ran at load 40 to 95 on 12 cores. Default 5 s timeouts and some describe-level 20 to 30 s timeouts failed on pristine code (sessions.test.ts, restore-scan.test.ts, lovejoin.test.ts:1111). Later runs used --testTimeout=120000, with explicit test timeouts scaled ×10 in the copies only. I checked every 'caught' result against its failure message. One false catch, M54's first run (a timeout that pristine code also hits under this load), was discarded and rerun. The final fire-run logs had no failures at all (52 + 57 files passed).

tests/chain-reservations.test.ts:59 (L27) no longer produces the race its comment describes. Under the StalePool mutant, the return drew 10 of the 20 pool boxes and the public mix drew 8, with zero overlap, in four runs. With the pool cut to 17 boxes the draws were 8 and 8, again with no overlap. The two chains never draw from the same reservations, so the test can't fail without the check; lovejoin-share-review-fixes.test.ts:571 is what pins it.

Several lane-named tests don't pin their guard: chain-reservations:59 (a1), lovejoin-not-enough (a13), public-mix-start (b11, b12), lovejoin-flows and lovejoin-1-5-0 (b14), chain-reservations:111 (it pins only the public mix's copy of the unreserve, checked() at 4976-4985), lovejoin-chain-review-fixes (b15), lovejoin-accounts (b16), public-mix-unsure (b17) and lovejoin-bring-review-fixes (a4/b18, which pins Bring one back's own reserved refusal). collateral-held, lovejoin-launch-review-fixes and lovejoin-accounts-review-fixes are UI tests that never reach the worker.

The CHAIN_SPENT_TRIES cap (lovejoin.ts:265) is pinned only by a hang. Without the cap, the send loop retries a spent transaction on fake sleeps that never yield to a timer, so Vitest's own timeout never fires either. CI would hang rather than fail. A unit assertion would pin it cleanly: chainRetryMs(1, { busy: 0, spent: CHAIN_SPENT_TRIES }, new SpentInputError('x')) should return undefined.

coverage: Tried every guard in E1a's and E1b's lists, after merging the duplicates (a1/b13, a4/b18, a5/b22, a6/b24, a7/b25, and a9 with b14). That is 37 guards and 71 mutants, run in the order asked: no named test first, then a stranger's or site's input, then the rest. Every mutant ran against its lane-named tests where the lane named any. Every survivor then ran against each test where the fire marker showed its guard acting; for M01, M02, M03, M09, M14, M62 and M68, against every test that reaches the line as well. Not fire-checked: 43 of the 192 reaching test files, which reach the modules only through handlers, sessions, sw or dapp and never call a Lovejoin flow (accounts*, dapp-*, governance, swap-*, wallet, worker and similar). Their runs could miss a firing, but none of them calls a Lovejoin flow. Two runs were cut short. M24's extra reach-set run (65 tests) was stopped after 15 minutes under load with no failure, though its marker never fired, so it couldn't catch. M54's runs were stopped while hanging; see the notes. Not run: Playwright, Rust (no guard here is in Rust, and none sits behind WebAssembly), any WebAssembly rebuild, and the verifiers' r51-* tests, which I excluded from every run.
